meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son's grade changed on his phone before anyone picked up a phone to call me.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing that down. "Like, being stuck" isn't a wrong answer, Hale, and a student not naming a scene in the moment isn't proof of anything. Show me the note you wrote that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Okay. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's what an outline is for. Put the October 15 outline next to the essay and turn them toward me.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing today, not Friday. You still haven't put the outline in front of me, so a rewrite for what, Hale? And the zero comes out of the gradebook now, not after Thursday.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record, and you said you would put that in writing by Friday at 3 PM. I still want the zero out of the gradebook now, the terms in writing, and the October 15 outline set next to the essay where I can read both. I expect it in writing today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, still wanting the zero withdrawn, and she has not accepted the rewrite; your offer matches the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4), but she wants it in writing today and wants to see your documents first, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one sentence and went straight to your reasons, which earned a flat okay and a real question instead of an attack.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite while she had asked twice to see the outline and the essay side by side and you had not shown them, so she read the offer as a deal with no evidence behind it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed on a November 2 conversation and an October 15 outline, so it did not come near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked you to turn the outline and essay toward her, show them first and let her read the missing cowardice argument herself before you put the rewrite on the table.
